title: P0/P1 completion accepted finding IDs unbound to the first-pass review or attested file
observed_behavior: At the vulnerable discovery hash, an attestation for one reviewed file could claim a P1 located only on another file and absent from the first-pass row; both validation and completion returned no findings. At the final lock, exact finding-set equality, location-scoped membership, and location-scoped P0/P1 completion reject that construction.
expected_invariant: Every independent disposition must match the current first-pass finding set and be located on the attested current-hash path; an unrelated attestation cannot satisfy P0/P1 completion.
root_cause: The original attestation join checked central ID existence and global union coverage but did not bind claimed IDs to the first-pass row or finding locations.
failure_scenario: A reviewer attaches all P0/P1 IDs to one valid high-risk file and strict completion reports full disposition coverage without independent review of the affected paths.
evidence: Final source lines 1601-1627 enforce first-pass set equality, duplicate rejection, central disposition agreement, and path-local finding scope.
Final source lines 1657-1676 require each P0/P1 record to be covered by an attestation on one of its own location paths.
Final regression lines 907-930 reject mismatched first-pass sets, unrelated locations, and false global completion.
The final adversarial probe reproduced all three rejection messages and the 33-test module passed.
existing_safeguards: Attestations remain bound to current path, hash, worker, achieved first-pass status, and distinct canonical reviewer identities.
Claimed finding IDs and dispositions are validated against the central ledger.
safeguard_gap: Confirmed historical gap; resolved in the final implementation by exact first-pass and location-scoped joins.
tests_present: P0/P1 completion rejection when no location-scoped attestation exists.
tests_missing: No known final-lock regression gap was found during independent rereview.
recommended_remediation: Retain the exact finding-set equality and path-scoped completion joins, and keep the adversarial mismatch tests in the mandatory audit-ledger suite.
remediation_risk: medium: future schema changes must preserve multi-location scope semantics and historical fragment compatibility
validation_rung: Adversarial pure-function probes, full 33-test audit-ledger suite, Ruff, py_compile, live current-universe reconstruction, and exact SHA-256 lock.
prior_audit_relationship: Confirmed incomplete SR-005 remediation discovered during independent rereview; resolved and independently verified at the final lock.

title: First-pass review rows could cite phantom finding and error IDs without blocking completion
observed_behavior: At the discovery hash, a first-pass row could use syntactically valid but nonexistent finding_ids or error_ids, allowing an omitted P1 to disappear from the central completion set. The final implementation prepares central records first and rejects unknown, duplicate, or status-inconsistent IDs before applying reviews.
expected_invariant: Every first-pass finding and error ID must resolve to the deterministically prepared current ledgers, with no duplicates and exact agreement between review status and finding-list emptiness.
root_cause: First-pass fragment validation originally ran without current valid finding/error ID sets, and strict evidence validation lacked the referential join back to central records.
failure_scenario: A reviewer records line_reviewed_with_findings with a dummy finding ID while omitting the actual P1 fragment; strict completion sees no central P1 and publishes a false all-clear.
evidence: Final source lines 1494-1513 reject duplicate and unknown finding/error IDs and enforce no-findings versus with-findings consistency.
prepare_review_rows at lines 1680-1751 constructs current central ID sets before validating and merging first-pass records.
evidence_ledger_findings at lines 2240-2316 retains the joined validation in strict checking.
Regression lines 440-479 reject phantom finding and error IDs and contradictory no-findings status.
existing_safeguards: Finding and error fragments have schemas and unique-ID validation.
line_reviewed_with_findings requires at least one finding ID.
safeguard_gap: Confirmed historical gap; resolved by preparing and joining exact central ID sets before first-pass review application.
tests_present: No-findings status with nonempty finding list rejection.
tests_missing: No known final-lock referential-integrity regression gap was found during independent rereview.
recommended_remediation: Preserve preparation order and exact membership joins whenever finding, error, or review schemas evolve.
remediation_risk: medium: historical IDs must remain historical provenance rather than being inserted into current ID arrays
validation_rung: Adversarial fragment joins, deterministic reconstruction, full 33-test audit-ledger suite, Ruff, py_compile, and exact SHA-256 lock.
prior_audit_relationship: Confirmed completion-bypass root discovered while tracing the first-pass side of HIR-001; resolved and independently verified at the final lock.

title: Windows path aliases could evade repository identity and finding root-cause deduplication
observed_behavior: At the discovery hash, trailing-dot and trailing-space aliases could resolve to the same Windows object while retaining different lexical fingerprints; follow-up probing also covered ADS colons, reserved names including superscript digits, 8.3 aliases, and case-colliding Git paths. The final implementation rejects these ambiguous identities before evidence construction.
expected_invariant: Every accepted repository-relative path must have one portable Windows identity so containment, Git inventory, location joins, and root-cause fingerprints cannot disagree.
root_cause: The original path parser enforced general traversal constraints but omitted Windows component normalization and alias hazards, while Git-path identity was not casefold-unique.
failure_scenario: Two records name the same Windows object through canonical and aliased spellings, splitting deduplication or letting one spelling bypass current-file and location-scope evidence.
evidence: Final source lines 463-482 reject trailing dot or space, Windows-invalid characters, ADS colons, and reserved device stems including superscript forms.
Final source lines 485-503 reject resolved identity mismatches such as materialized 8.3 aliases.
Final git_blob_map lines 537-566 reject casefold-colliding index paths and ambiguous stages.
Regression lines 669-705 cover parent, trailing dot/space, ADS, CON, COM¹, LPT³, and available 8.3 aliases; lines 185-190 cover Git case collisions.
existing_safeguards: Absolute, parent, dot, empty, drive-qualified, and resolved-outside-root paths were already rejected.
safeguard_gap: Confirmed historical Windows normalization gap; resolved by portable lexical checks, resolved-identity checks, and casefold Git uniqueness.
tests_present: ADS and reserved-device rejection including superscript digits.
tests_missing: The 8.3 test is correctly conditional on the volume exposing that alias; no deterministic cross-volume materialization guarantee is possible.
recommended_remediation: Retain portable lexical validation and casefold uniqueness as shared identity gates before hashing, joining, or fingerprinting paths.
remediation_risk: low: repository evidence paths are Windows-first and should already use portable names
validation_rung: Pure path tests, live Windows alias probes, full 33-test audit-ledger suite, Ruff, py_compile, and exact SHA-256 lock.
prior_audit_relationship: Confirmed incomplete Windows-specific SR-003 remediation; resolved and independently verified at the final lock.

title: Unresolved Git index paths could be inventoried without a unique stage-0 identity
observed_behavior: During the initial SR-007 remediation, a tracked worktree-present path could be hashed even when Git exposed only non-stage-0 conflict entries and no authoritative blob identity. The final parser rejects unresolved stages, duplicate stage-0 entries, and casefold collisions before row construction, while build and freshness require mode-specific stage-0 provenance.
expected_invariant: Every tracked coverage row must have exactly one unambiguous stage-0 Git mode and object identity; unresolved or duplicate index states fail closed before any current-content claim.
root_cause: Tracked membership and worktree availability were originally treated as sufficient even when the index map had no unique stage-0 entry.
failure_scenario: A conflicted path with stages 1, 2, or 3 and a materialized worktree file is hashed as current content and strict completion publishes against a repository state with no uniquely defined tracked version.
evidence: Final git_blob_map lines 537-566 reject every nonzero stage and duplicate stage-0 path before returning the map.
Final build_rows lines 894-1062 require mode-dispatched index provenance for every tracked row.
Final current_content_findings lines 2176-2223 compare the current stage-0 map and mode against recorded evidence.
Regression lines 172-190 deterministically reject unresolved, duplicate stage-0, and casefold-ambiguous index records.
A final live probe reconstructed all 76 absent-worktree tracked rows from stage-0 Git blobs with nonempty content hashes and zero freshness findings.
existing_safeguards: Tracked paths come from Git index queries.
Worktree and Git-object hashes are recorded with explicit content_source and mode.
safeguard_gap: Confirmed historical fail-open index-state gap; resolved by fail-closed stage parsing and mode-aware construction/freshness checks.
tests_missing: A live conflicted-index integration fixture remains optional defense in depth; the parser branches are deterministically covered.
recommended_remediation: Keep unresolved-index rejection ahead of inventory and require unique stage-0 provenance for every tracked path regardless of worktree presence.
remediation_risk: low to medium: the audit intentionally refuses to run during unresolved merges
validation_rung: Adversarial index-record tests, live Git-blob reconstruction, full 33-test audit-ledger suite, Ruff, py_compile, and exact SHA-256 lock.
prior_audit_relationship: Confirmed incomplete SR-007 Git-index fallback edge case; resolved and independently verified at the final lock.

title: Tracked symlink and gitlink modes lacked safe, explicit evidence semantics
observed_behavior: At the vulnerable candidate hash, a mode-120000 path could be followed and attested as target bytes while recording the link blob identity, and mode-160000 attempted blob reads without explicit gitlink semantics. The final implementation dispatches by Git mode, hashes symlink payloads from the index, represents gitlinks by commit identity, rejects regular-mode worktree links, and never hashes an unsafe resolved path.
expected_invariant: Coverage and freshness semantics must derive from tracked Git mode: symlinks bind to link payload without target traversal, gitlinks bind to commit identity, regular modes reject links, and unsafe or unknown modes fail closed.
root_cause: The initial implementation branched on materialized Path behavior before Git mode, allowing pathlib target following and leaving gitlinks without a non-blob identity policy.
failure_scenario: A tracked symlink points outside the repository and the audit hashes external target bytes, potentially exposing data and publishing evidence that matches neither the tracked link blob nor a repository-contained regular file.
evidence: Final build_rows lines 894-1062 dispatch regular blobs, symlink blobs, gitlinks, unsafe paths, and unsupported modes explicitly.
Final current_content_findings lines 2176-2223 repeats mode-aware freshness checks and rejects source or mode transitions.
Final finding validation lines 1233-1387 permits index-backed symlink and gitlink locations without following a worktree target while preserving line-bound checks where applicable.
Regression lines 560-627 prove symlink payload hashing, gitlink commit identity, mode-change detection, and regular-mode symlink rejection.
Regression lines 707-743 prove ancestor containment and that unsafe resolved paths never reach sha256_file.
existing_safeguards: Resolved repository containment and stage-0 object identities are recorded.
The live repository currently has no special Git modes, limiting immediate exposure.
safeguard_gap: Confirmed historical mode-dispatch and read-boundary gap; resolved by explicit special-mode semantics and safe resolved-worktree checks.
tests_missing: A live-platform symlink and submodule fixture remains optional defense in depth; deterministic special-mode branches are covered.
recommended_remediation: Keep Git mode authoritative, never follow worktree links for evidence, and retain explicit fail-closed behavior for unknown modes or unsafe resolved paths.
remediation_risk: medium: filesystem and Git mode behavior varies by platform, so mode semantics must remain deterministic and index-derived
validation_rung: Mocked special-mode adversarial probes, resolved-boundary tests, live mode census, full 33-test audit-ledger suite, Ruff, py_compile, and exact SHA-256 lock.
prior_audit_relationship: Confirmed incomplete SR-007 special-mode provenance remediation; resolved and independently verified at the final lock.
